variant_reviews.comparison: For p0335 (2.5), retain the hierarchical prior, disjoint model tags, parameter map T and likelihood p_n(T(theta),Y). Build the normalized withDensity measure on positive finite evidence. posterior supplies a conditional-law kernel after proving standard Borel/nonempty parameter space and finite measurable sampling kernel; its almost-everywhere density theorem is not an unconditional samplewise identity or a convention at zero/infinite evidence. It does not select a variational minimizer.

For p0519 (16), form the dependent Markov-path likelihood product p_D,f(X_(i-1)D,X_iD), retaining the explicit joint Borel measurability and B in S. The initial law is common to all parameters; its cancellation does not make path observations iid. Identify the sampling kernel’s predictive-relative density with this likelihood divided by its prior integral before applying posterior_eq_withDensity. Keep f coordinates distinct from theta coordinates used for other posterior expectations, and justify the version when evaluating under a fixed true diffusivity law.

For p1433 D11, posterior directly provides the structural conditional law of f given X once the function parameter space is nonempty standard Borel and the model is a measurable finite kernel. Dominated Bayes formula requires the corresponding measurable density representation and normalizer identification. The paper analyzes the result under fixed P_f0^(n), not the prior predictive law; an almost-everywhere posterior identity under the latter does not alone justify every true-law statement or supply function-space posterior contraction.

For p1691 D12, the prior is on probability measures on R^d and may depend on n. Use the n-fold product convolution-density likelihood f_Y(Y_i), not a likelihood for directly observed signals, and prove measurability of the law-valued parameterization and positive finite evidence. The regular-kernel construction needs the corresponding standard Borel realization; posterior_eq_withDensity gives a predictive-almost-everywhere identity after density identification. Later posteriors of observation laws require a measurable convolution pushforward rather than a new prior or silently identifying signal and observation laws.

For p1825 (21), weight the Gaussian prior on initial states V by exp(-one-half the sum of squared Euclidean R^2 residuals) and supply its marginal normalizer. Keep the source u_theta(X_i,t_i) argument ordering as printed, including the recorded discrepancy with model (19). The resulting kernel is a posterior for the nonlinear PDE observation experiment after measurability/space proofs; the generic constructor does not assert it is Gaussian or prove MCMC behavior. variant_reviews.comparison: For p1178 use the unconditional complete test-pair law P_Q for (X,Y), set mu=Measure.map X P_Q and eta(x) to the conditional-label kernel mass at {1}. The feature domain is R^d and the label space is binary; do not condition eta on the missingness pattern or replace X by its zero-filled observed projection. The kernel is a probability distribution and yields the correct regression identity almost everywhere. Later missingness and smoothness conditions are imposed at all support points, so the library’s arbitrary values on null fibers do not by themselves satisfy those pointwise conditions or resolve the source version convention.

For p1433 retain X in [0,1]^d, d≥1, and independent observations from the common pair law. h0(x) is the success mass of condDistrib Y X under that law; the ordinary definition does not require a logistic prior, though a later map constructs one. Use the appropriate cube subtype and measurable coordinates. The binary conditional law can be represented as bernoulliMeasure 1 0 h0(x) after bounding the kernel mass, but independence of sampled pairs remains separate from the one-pair conditional law. No multivariate wavelet basis or dimension-dependent contraction rate is supplied by these APIs.

variant_reviews.comparison: For each fixed alternative g, the inner infimum/max is an absolute-error decision problem for the location Z(h), h in {f,g}, under the white-noise laws with noise epsilon; only afterwards take the supremum over g. minimaxRisk uses extended nonnegative risk and the correct inf-estimator/sup-parameter order for that inner problem, but its estimators are all Markov kernels. Establish equivalence with the paper's admissible estimator convention or restrict explicitly to deterministic measurable functions; do not assume randomized and deterministic optimization coincide. One estimator is shared by the two laws, but may depend on the fixed pair because its infimum is inside the outer supremum. Preserve infinite risks using lintegral; no attainment or global inf-estimator/sup-all-functions equality follows.

Instantiate the two-point absolute minimizer-location loss with the fixed-design Gaussian regression sampling law on n+1 observations and noise sigma. Its outer supremum over g remains outside the pair-specific estimator infimum. The generic minimaxRisk quantifies Markov-kernel estimators; identification with the printed infimum needs the estimator-class bridge, and an extended integral avoids giving nonintegrable losses the Bochner fallback value zero. Do not substitute the white-noise experiment, squared loss or one estimator optimized uniformly over the entire convex class.
